claims.explanation: Fludroxycortide is a glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative/killing pattern likely reflects glucocorticoid receptor signaling competence: lines with intact NR3C1 expression and an active glucocorticoid transcriptional program are sensitized, while lines with low NR3C1 expression or mutations in NR3C1 or its coactivators/context (e.g., PTEN loss, EGFR-driven lung lines) are protected. The enrichment of NRAS/BRAF-mutant melanoma and PIK3CA/PTEN-altered lines among sensitive lines suggests that MAPK/PI3K pathway activation may cooperate with GR-mediated apoptosis, whereas EGFR-mutant NSCLC and Ewing sarcoma lines are relatively resistant.

features.basis: GR agonist drug; target expression required for response
loss-of-function mutations in the drug target would abrogate GR signaling
PTEN loss/PI3K activation observed in sensitive lines (ZR751, FTC133, HEC265)
PIK3CA mutations enriched in sensitive lines (MKN1, SNU840, HGC27, SNUC5)
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines among most killed (LOXIMVI, K029AX, HEC265)
NRAS-mutant lines among most killed (KU1919, IPC298)
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines among least affected (NCIH1650, NCIH1648, HCC4006)
TP53 mutations common in both groups but enriched in resistant lines; p53 loss may blunt GR-induced apoptosis
ARID1A mutations in several sensitive lines (LOXIMVI, KU1919, HEC265, SNUC5)
NF1 loss/RAS activation in sensitive lines (LOXIMVI, FTC133, S117, BICR6)
FBXW7 mutations in sensitive lines (MKN1, CL11, SNUC5)
CBG expression may sequester glucocorticoid and reduce intracellular drug availability
